title: ops-sync-hypothesis-notes-2026-08-02
body:
Context and goal:
- Prep notes for weekly SRE ops sync (30m). Focus: short briefing for execs + working-level action triage.
- Want to leave meeting with 3 concrete follow-ups: (1) low-noise paging plan, (2) SLO adjustment proposal, (3) incident mitigation runbook updates.

Quick TL;DR (for first 5 mins):
- Paging noise up ~18% week-over-week; most increase from model-serve GC pauses and a new lambda flapping in EU region.
- SLO burn observed on embeddings endpoint during peak window (17:05-17:45 UTC) — 94.2% availability vs 99% target.
- Two high-severity incidents last week: 2026-07-25 (serve GC cascade) and 2026-07-27 (config rollout causing region split).

Key evidence and quick queries to show live:
- Rolling 7d p50/p95 latency for /v1/generate: Query: metrics-dashboard -> v1_generate_latency?range=7d&quantiles=50,95
- Paging rate by service: metrics -> paging.rate{service:*}. Top sources: model-serve, edge-proxy, lambda-eu
- Error-rate spikes: logs -> count(status>=500) group_by service, hour

Hypotheses (that we should test in sync):
1) GC/heap growth for a handful of model-serve pods is causing tail latency and cascading retries -> leads to increased pages from alerting policy 'model-serve-high-latency'.
   - Quick check: compare heap usage/top ten pods by restarts in last 48h (kubectl top / k8s dashboard).
2) A recent config change to routing table caused a small percentage of requests to hit a non-quantized model variant in EU -> higher latency and memory footprint.
   - Check rollout PR: GH #2145 (linked).
3) Alert thresholds are too sensitive for transient CPU spikes; need a short cooling window (3m->10m) to reduce noise.

Incident briefs (one-liners to read aloud):
- 2026-07-25 - serve GC cascade: root cause suspected contiguous allocation pattern after new tokenizers merged in PR 2109. Symptoms: p95 CPU/heap increase, slow autovac GC, followed by pod restarts and cascading retry storms. Impact: ~7% reduction in global throughput for 32 minutes.
- 2026-07-27 - config rollout: routing policy change (region affinity flag) rolled without canary; ~12% of EU traffic routed to older model variant causing increased tail latency and contributor pages. Impact: degraded embeddings SLO for EU customers (one customer alert escalated).

Paging trend notes (scratch table):
- Baseline avg pages/day (June weekly avg): 42
- Last 7 days avg pages/day: 50 (+19%)
- Top pager sources: model-serve (45%), edge-proxy (25%), infra-lambda (18%), other (12%)
- Top hours for pages: 17:00-18:00 UTC (peak), 03:00-04:00 UTC (GC window)

SLO status summary to present:
- embeddings.v1.availability: target 99.0% -> current 94.2% (rolling 7d) -> immediate mitigation required
- generate.v1.latency.p95: target 350ms -> current 410ms during peak 17:05-17:45
- kv-cache.hit-rate: target 60% -> current 58% (small regression after caching tweak)

Proposed short-term mitigations (talking points + owners):
1) Immediate rollback of region-affinity routing flag for EU (owner: Marco Diaz) - ETA 2h to rollback, test, and monitor.
2) Emergency GC-tuning on flagged model-serve pod group: bump young gen limit, enable concurrent sweeping (owner: Alex Chen + infra) - ETA 6h for staged rollout.
3) Temporarily increase alert window on 'model-serve-high-latency' from 3m to 10m to reduce noise (owner: Priya Rao) - ETA 1h to change policy and validate.
4) Add synthetic probe in 17:00-18:00 UTC slot for embeddings endpoint (owner: SLO-ops oncall) - ETA 24h.

Longer-term actions and owners (capture in ticket backlog):
- Deep mem-profiling of model-serve with new tokenizers (owner: applied-ml team) - link to JIRA-OPS-9876.
- Canary + automated rollback for routing feature flags (owner: platform-engineering) - PR checklist update required.
- Re-evaluate SLOs for embeddings with tiered targets (hosted vs dedicated) (owner: product-hosted-api) - propose in next SLO review.

Meeting agenda (30m):
- 0-5m: TL;DR + top incidents (read aloud)
- 5-12m: Data deep-dive (paging trend graph, SLO slides) - Priya runs metrics
- 12-20m: Triage decisions (rollbacks, GC tuning) - assign owners and deadlines
- 20-27m: Communication plan (customer comms + release notes)
- 27-30m: Quick retrospective + confirm follow-ups

Notes to self (things to surface if asked):
- Impact quantification: convert 7d availability delta into estimated dollar-impact for hosted customers (rough calc: requests per minute * %failed * avg revenue per request) - good to have if execs ask.
- If asked about recurrence: show correlation of new PR merges vs pages (simple table).
- Keep debugging trace ids handy: trace ids for two incidents: trace-0a1b2c and trace-4f5g6h.

Follow-up action list (to capture as JIRA tickets during meeting):
- JIRA-OPS-9901: Rollback EU routing flag + run post-rollback synthetic tests (owner: Marco Diaz) - due 2026-08-02 18:00 UTC
- JIRA-OPS-9902: GC tuning experiment + monitor p95 (owner: Alex Chen) - due 2026-08-03 12:00 UTC
- JIRA-OPS-9903: Alert-window change for model-serve-high-latency (owner: Priya Rao) - due 2026-08-02 15:00 UTC
- JIRA-OPS-9904: Add 17:00 UTC synthetic probe for embeddings (owner: SLO-ops oncall) - due 2026-08-03 09:00 UTC

Open questions (to resolve in sync):
- Do we want to permanently relax the latency alert window to 10m, or only during EMERGENCY windows?
- Should embeddings SLO be region-aware (different targets for eu vs us)?
- Is the tokenizer change the true root cause of GC pattern or a coincident contributor? Need memprofiles.

Quick communication draft (for customer-facing Slack/email if needed):
- Short: "We observed transient latency and availability degradation impacting embeddings during a peak window. Root cause investigation in progress; immediate rollback/mitigation underway. We'll follow up with impact summary and timeline for a permanent fix."

Misc scratch ideas (future experiments):
- Canary thermal test: deliberate load generator to a single pool to surface GC patterns pre-merge.
- Adaptive alert suppression using recent pages history to avoid escalation loops.

End notes:
- Bring these notes into main confluence page after sync and attach SLO graphs.
- Tag PRs and incidents in the follow-up tickets for traceability.

-- Alex
